host_identification_status.warning: Scores and confidence bands are heuristic, not calibrated probabilities. Opening/closing phrase lists are incomplete and currently English-oriented; translated ASR text can affect cues. Manually verify predictions and evaluate across known-host episodes.

methodology.transcript_scope: full transcript; not limited to overlapping speech
methodology.context_policy: Each response turn is assessed with up to 5 preceding different-speaker turns.
methodology.moderator_policy: Moderation, panelist introductions, summaries, follow-up questions, and repetition without a stance are neutral; substantive anchor stances are classified normally. Host identity is not used for classification.
methodology.overlap_policy: Overlap and interruption are not evidence of stance by themselves.
methodology.neutral_policy: Neutral candidates are counted in the candidate summary but omitted from interaction records; uncertain records are retained.
methodology.target_policy: Target is a specific earlier turn; no reverse inference. Response timestamp determines subtopic mapping.
limitations: ASR errors can affect stance and exact quote matching.
The analysis does not infer intent, ideology, bias, or factual correctness.

episode_summary.ratio_note: Agreement family = agreement + partial_agreement; disagreement family = disagreement + counterargument. Neutral turns are omitted; uncertain cases are excluded from ratio denominators.

interactions.reasoning: The speaker responds to the anchor's challenge regarding contradictions by offering their primary goal of defeating the BJP as the underlying rationale for their political actions.

interactions.reasoning: The speaker counters the host's point regarding vote percentages and impact in Bihar/Bengal by reiterating that their primary effect is disproportionate media projection and polarization.

speaker_turn_interval_audit.recovered_text: So what does this new political equation mean? Let's cut across to our panelists this evening. Joining me, Ashutosh Otha, political analyst, Varis Patan, spokesperson, AIMIM, Rajvath Setri, political analyst, Juhi Singh, spokesperson, Samajwadi Party, Tuhin Sinha, BJP national spokesperson. Let's begin with a party which stands to technically lose the most, Samajwadi Party. And Juhi Singh, what does this new equation mean for the Samajwadi Party?

For us, asset means nothing. As you said that technically people are perceiving that we stand to lose, but if this alliance thinks that they can counter the BJP and they're there to defeat the BJP, they can hold the BJP accountable for whatever misdeeds, misrules, misinformation the BJP has spread. It's been years in UP. then it's fine with us, because they have to decide what their strategy is, how they are going to work, what is their seed-sharing formula. Instead of drawing a report card for the Samajwadi Party, which I think many of their members do as per convenience, I think it's high-cut that they drew a accountability report card for the BJP, talk about the issues, whether it's unemployment, whether it's farmers' distress, it's women's security.

You're saying nothing to lose despite the fact that AIMIM just about a month ago in an open letter had said let's form an alliance in Uttar Pradesh which you had rebuffed. So you are saying you don't need them.

I don't think it worked out. I mean, I don't know what the proposal came. We are working on our boot levels on our SIR list, which are totally faulty. The Chief Minister of UP himself is saying that people are missing from the voters list. That's a huge number, and that has to be corrected. All right.
Okay, Tuhin Sinha, some would suggest good news coming in for the BJP, another team B-C of the BJP in Uttar Pradesh this time.

Well, good evening Pritik, good evening everybody. This new alliance is another reason why BJP is headed towards a massive, massive win. But no, they're not RP team, they're not RC team. Point is that Asaduddin Awaisi, as they say in Hindi, is Begani Shadime Abdullah Diwana. He's the same Begani Shadime Abdullah Diwana everywhere. So, anybody he aligns with, anybody who chooses to align with him must be in a position of desperation. Otherwise, nobody gives him any importance anywhere. But, equally, if you look at this alliance, the Muslim votes might gravitate towards AIMIM today, because Akhilesh Yadav seems to be taking the community for granted. One day, he says he will go to Ayodhya. The other day, he says he will go to Kashi. The third day, he says he will go to some other temple. So he has been taking the Muslim community for granted, leading to some amount of confusion, which the AIMIM wants to encash on. But the Dalit vote will walk away from Mr. Ravan, once Mr. Ravan decides to go ahead with AIMIM, because the Daleks per se don't identify with this rather unnatural alliance. And that is where the other side will stand to lose both ways. You know, the Muslim vote goes to, gets divided. They don't get Dalit vote. So I think we are headed towards a massive, massive win. Very similar to... All right. Okay. Varus Pathan,

allow me to bring you in. Varus Pathan, you've managed to play the spoiler in a state like Bihar and even in a state... Okay. Do we have Varus Pathan? Okay, we don't seem to have Varus Patan. We're going to try and connect to Varus Patan. Let me bring in till then Ashutosh as well as Rajat Sethi into the mix. Ashutosh, what do you make of this? Because the AIMIM Asaduddin Ovesi has played a spoiler in Bihar in Bengal, but history stands testimony he hasn't been able to make in roads in the state of Uttar Pradesh. It's not the first election. He's fighting there. On the other hand, you have Chandrasekhar Azad, who did fairly well. He won his seat of Nagina in general elections having said that, his alliance with another party, the JJP in Haryana failed abysmally in Haryana elections.

See, Preeti, this is all about Dalit votes in Uttar Pradesh. This is not all about the Muslim votes. So I am not surprised that OIC has aligned with Chandrasekhar and projected him as the chief ministerial candidate. And everybody knows that until very recently, the UP election has been triangular, other four-angular election kind of a thing. It has been turned into a bipolar election. And Mayavati's vote share has been shrinking rapidly, especially in the parliament election, where she was reduced to percent vote share and a drop of almost more than percent vote share. So, but where this vote share or where the Dalit voter is going will decide the election in this election, because if you look at the figures of parliament election, almost to of the non-jato voter which is substantial in UP, has gone to the India Gatbandhan, and slightly, around has gone to the India Gatbandhan. Whereas the Jato Vartan, which has been basically, have been very committed to the Mayawati personally, there is also a a drift there, goes to the BJP and goes to the Samajwadi party. Now, it is this of the Dalit voters which is going to swing election either in favor of Samajwadi party or in favor of the BJP. Most probably, if you take election as a benchmark, the possibility is that this might go to the India-Katbandhan. So this entire exercise is to stop that drift from BSP to Samajwadi party in the Congress Gadbandhan. That's what I see the selection. And OIC is just a spoiler, as he always think he is. His game worked in Bihar, but I don't think he's... But it hasn't ever worked in

Uttar Pradesh. Till now, it hasn't worked in Uttar Pradesh. It worked in Bihar. It also, I would think, worked in Bengal as well in pockets. It did fairly well as a spoiler. Okay, I want to bring in... Do we have Mr. Varas Patan in this conversation?

Do we have Mr. Varis Patan? Okay, we do have, Mr. Pathan, you're back with us. Some would want to understand what is the AIMM's thinking behind aligning with Chandrasekhar Azad, especially because your party hasn't done quite well in Uttar Pradesh. You've aligned with Chandrasekhar Azad. There is clear amount of bonhomie with your leader as well as Jayan Chaudhary, who's RLD as well. So one doesn't quite understand where the AIMIM stands this election.

Well, ma'am, today is a very historic day in the politics of Uttar Pradesh, where in our party, Majlis-Ettihad Muslimin and MP Chandrasekhar Azad's party, the Azad Samaj party, today form an alliance and call it Samajik Parivartan Murcha. Now, see, our intention and our motive was to ensure that the BJP is defeated and to ensure that they don't form the government the third time. We had requested earlier today to come along with us, form an alliance, and let us defeat the BJP. But the so-called secular parties, they did not do anything. They just kept their mouth shut. And so today we have formed an alliance. And I am sure and I am confident that many of them will be having sleepless nights from today. because since so many years they have been taking the votes of the Muslims, Dalits and the minorities and what did they do for betterment of the political empire? But Mr.
Padhan, your party has never worked in UP. Things have never really gone in your favour in the state of Gupta Pradesh.
False. These are totally false and baseless allegations which are... No sir, I am only
looking at past track record. How is it false?
No, no. What is the Congress' first track record? And what did the Samaritans... Sir, better than
yours. Better than yours in Uttar Pradesh. What is
the Samaritans' first track record? They lost almost all the elections in four times. But sir, you
haven't been able to win a single seat.
This was the same thing which was being told to us during the Bihar election as well, and we won five seats in Bihar? Sir, you have

always done... No, no. No, no, no. One second, sir. To put this in perspective, you have always done well in the state of Bihar. You've always had a bit of a vote share and resonance and presence. The AIMMM in the last election in UP was less than vote, sir. Less than vote, and you could not convert even one seat.

But this time, you see, we will be winning. Many of our candidates will win. They will be elected assembly and they will raise their voice for the Dalits, for the Muslims, for the people who have been taken just for granted by the so-called secular parties. What I have been saying since the beginning is very true. On one side, we have got the BJP, on the other side, we have got the Samajwadi and the Congress, the so-called secular parties. The two sides of the same coin, they have been playing... Then why are you
inviting the Samajwadi party and the Congress to come and join you?

The BJP is playing hard in the politics. The Samajwadi and the secular people, they were soft in the politics. We know they are the... enemies of Muslims. Here also what we are seeing Akhilesh now going to Ayodhya.
Okay. But sir I don't understand. I want to bring in Rajan Sethi because your argument has come back to you sir.
Allow me seconds. Allow me seconds. Please.
Of course.
I would like to ask a simple question to the Samajwadi party spokespersons, especially to the Muslim MLAs and the MPs. What is their take and what is their say on Akhiles Yadav visiting Ayodhya?

They won't say. They are not saying. What have they got to say now? See, that is why we say you took the name of, you took the votes of, this is the name of secularism. But, sir, but how do you see that? We are fighting for the protection of the community.
And so we have founded an alliance. Okay,
I have understood your point. Sir, I understand your point but allow me to ask you because at one end you are saying
that Samajwadi party is anti-Muslim. On the other hand, from stage you have given an invitation to the Samajwadi party to join forces with you. How do the two add up?

This was the same thing we told them during the Bihar elections also because they... that because we contest elections, they lose elections and all blah, blah, blah, they want... Sir, are you okay to join hands with the
Samajwadi party who you say is anti-Muslim and the Congress who you call is the other side of the same coin of the BJP?
Madam, our intention aim is to ensure that the BJP does not form the government for the third time. We want to defeat the BJP. That is why
we told them. Okay, you made
your point sir. Fair point. So it doesn't matter, you will even join hands with an anti-Muslim party and a BJP team to defeat the BJP.
Our alliance has today declared Mr. Chandrasekhar Azad as the Chief Minister candidate of Uttar Pradesh. I hear
you, sir.
Allow me to bring in Rajat Sethi, sir. Allow me to open up the
panel.
Okay, allow me to bring in Rajat Sethi. Rajat, as a political analyst, what do you make of what's just happened?

So Priti ji, I think there is no harm in any party starting with zero. MIM is almost at zero, and so is the Azad Samaj party also. Both of them have less than one lakh votes, roughly. Again, that does not go against them. We've also seen that what happens to this narrative of B team, C team, which has been labeled onto AIMIM right from West Bengal election to Bihar elections. That narrative, RJD and the Congress Party and the TMC kept on pushing and trying to push AIMM against the wall on this basic standpoint. But counter to that, what MIM and what Mr. Ovesi has been consistently saying is that, see, what happens to these MPs and MLAs that you elect on the ticket of Congress Party or you elect on the ticket of TMC? The moment they lose elections, or they lose power, they will switch. Those elected MPs and MLAs will switch over and go and join the BJP. One of the biggest narrative of Mr. Obaisi has been Congress Party in the state of Bihar. Currently, there are six MLAs and out of six, five were at the verge of joining the BJP. The talks were finished and everything, it was all in public domain. So today, OIC can stand up and say that, see, even if you elect these people, none of these people are going to fight for your interest and they'll cross party and go and join the BJP. So therefore, this chorus of calling them a C team, et cetera, of the BJP only has so much of shelf life. After that, the Muslims will start looking at what is in it for them when they look at Samajwadi party or Congress party. Also, what happens is through this third front which has been created, they're calling it the first front, but I don't... I mean, even if they stand relevant in this entire election, that would be a good win for them. But I think one thing what it does is, it puts pressure on Congress party. Sorry, sir.
Okay. Sir, allow Rajat Sethu to finish. I'll come back to you. Mr. Sethu, make your point.

So, Preeti ji, what it does is it puts pressure on Congress party also because now Congress party doesn't have the elbow room to go out and negotiate with the Samajwadi party with the zeal that they have been showing so far. They would want to come out and try and staple together with the Samajwadi party alliance, so much so that the vote shape does not get further splintered into smaller groups. Clearly, Congress has had a very bad show in the previous election when they were independent of Samajwadi party. Looking at the bigger picture, the consolidation of this third front, and if they're able to add smaller parties into their fold, maybe they will be able to get three, four, five percent. They might not be able to win a single seat, but they can disturb the apple cart, which is sort of balancing it between the Congress and Samajwadi party on one side and the BJP on the other side.

Ashutosh I know you want to come in and I'm going to go around again once to everyone and I want to bring in Juhi Singh into this conversation from the Samajwadi party and Juhi Singh the fact is sometimes when it comes down to the micro detailing if you have an alliance of the AIMIM and The Azad Samaj Party, Chandrasekhar Azad, it will and could be a factor especially where West UP is concerned. You might speak of pockets but it very well could play as a huge factor there. You have Chandrasekhar Azad who has a fair amount of influence in the area and you know that better, ma'am. There are smaller alliances and other smaller parties which are part of the NDA where East UP is concerned. There's also now talks of smaller outfits coming up where Bundelkhand is concerned. All of them
taking away percentages of your vote bank could really harm you in the long run.

Preeti, I think we were prepared for that. I have been hearing the entire conversation. In the entire conversation of Varus Patanbhai, the only thing I could hear was what the Congress has done wrong, what the SP has done wrong, and how many elections we have lost. There is no mention of issues. And let's say I might not be a Muslim, but I do not think that they understand the Muslims of UP. What is the dichotomy of anybody going to Ram Madinah and the presumption of Waris Pathan that every Muslim would be offended because somebody visits the Ram Madinah? I mean, it's ridiculous. Secondly, they can go on their calculations. We are working on the ground. And as for the Dalit vote, Reservation has been taken away by the BJP, whether it is in government jobs, whether it is in the appointments of assistant professors, whether it is in the bharti, which we have seen. Nobody has done anything to rectify it. So, these are the issues and also the issues of rising fees, people being suspended from universities. not allowing to raise their voices. So yeah, they can talk about, the friendship is there with the BJP and it is very, very apparent. What did he or anybody, I would say that Shetty had to say about the BJP. It's all right. You know, but that was

exactly what was said in of the BSP. Yes, the BSP fell, the BSP shrunk, but it still managed to take a sizable vote percentage, ma'am. And that mattered in the long run for you. I'll come back to you. Why do

you think that they took away our vote percentage? I mean, maybe the BJP could have gone higher, it might have been there. Okay, it could have been. Fair point. And the Muslims too. So, I mean, we are working with them and we have a committed work. All right, let me, allow me to bring in.
Okay, final comments. And if I have time, I'll come back again. But Tuhin Sena, final comments, sir, on this new alliance.

Opposition parties are clearly feeling the heat. And that is when they go for desperate, unnatural alliances. So, clearly, they are in bad shape. And when Varish Patan says that we will ensure that the BJP gets defeated, let me just tell them that, no matter what all alliances they work out, they are incapable of beating it. But having said that, today, I think there is no difference between the Congress and the AIMIM. The AIMIM, in a big state like Bihar, the AIMIM won five seats. The Congress won six seats. So, in the municipal corporation elections of Maharashtra earlier this year, which included Mumbai, in at least three places, in at least three cities, AIMIM actually did better than the Congress Party. So, today, there is not much difference between the Congress Party and AIMIM. And if Khilesh Yadav had been a little more wise. Maybe he would have dumped Congress party and thought of an alliance with AIMIM. That's the hard reality, which I'm telling you.
All right. OK, let's get in final comments in if we have Mr. Varus Pathan. But if we don't, Ashutosh has been trying to make a point for a while. Go ahead, sir. Final comments.

See, Preeti, I think we are unnecessarily giving too much importance to this OIC party. You know, they draw their instance from Hyderabad, from Telangana. You know, in how many seats they contested? Only nine. Only nine. And what was the percentage of vote they got? In parliamentary elections, they got how many percentage of vote? And in A political party which does not contest even all the seats in Telangana now is arrogantly saying that they are going to defeat the BJP and the Samajmati party together in Uttar Pradesh. So now the issue is why they have entered into the race. They have entered into the race because they will get disproportionate projection in the TV channels. They will speak something, some provocative things, and that will help BJP polarize elections. That is their role. And that is why, despite political parties just getting two to three percent vote, even in Telangana, you will see them in all the TV channels. There will be a permanent fixture in all the TV channels, every time. And they will be asked questions. And the questions which they will answer will help polarize the politics across. So that is why they have entered into the race. And unfortunately or fortunately, Chandrasekhar has fallen into the trap with him.

But, you know, Ashutosh, and I'll come back, because, you know, you are saying, fortunately, unfortunately, Chandrasekhar's fallen in the trap with him, but Chandrasekhar did ally, similarly, maybe not with an AIMIM, but with the JJP in Haryana. Now, okay, at that point of time, the combination didn't quite fare well, but you speak of only Hyderabad, but the fact is, Overseas party has been able to make a fair amount of political capital in Bihar and even in Bengal, not getting many seats, but denting it for the principle opposition then.

Preeti, what percentage of votes they are getting is not important. Important is they are more than the out of proportion projection of AMIM, that they are going to, that they will talk something which will help a polarized election during the election. That's why I keep saying this. Why OSCE has been considered to be the Muslim leader? Why? Why every time something happened, people go with their mic and talk to him and get their reactions. And then the entire debate is mounted on that.
Entire debate is mounted on that, not on a daily basis.
Okay, final comments, Rajat
Sethi. There are many political parties who are getting two percent, three percent vote share across the country. We don't go to them because it doesn't help polarize elections.
Rajat Sethi, final comments coming.

So PPG, if voting percentage is any metric of media coverage, then Aam Aadmi Party when it was starting should have got zero media coverage then, right? Aam Aadmi Party was a non-entity in Gujarat, was a non-entity in Goa. They should have not gotten any kind of a media coverage. What kind of a retarded argument is this? If a party is there, they have all the rights. If they are making statements which are extreme in nature, it is media's responsibility not to cover them. I mean, where do you stop the political party from coming out and making comments? By that logic, Samajwadi party has made all kinds of obnoxious remarks as well, and so has BJP. So try and contain those remarks as well. So again, my point is not this. From a pure analysis perspective, as I said, Samajwadi party for instance, their PDA, it is trying to be one slogan, trying to be an over-encompassing, all-encompassing sort of a message where P is Pichhada also and Pandit also. The problem with this kind of a messaging is, no, Juhi ji, this is an honest assessment. You're trying to be pleasing to too many constituents together. And in this, in this sort of a setting,
Okay, allow him. So when you when you try to be everything to everyone, you end up just being a congressman. Just allow me to make you hear you on this.

So my point is that when the MIM and when Chandrasekhar Azad, they make more shrill arguments, they suddenly stand to draw a lot of attention because a Samajwadi party is trying to be too risk averse in its position. They had to go beyond the MY equation. And that has been their sort of plan and action for quite some time. But in that exercise, if you start going to Ayodhya, if you start going away from your core plans and your core messaging, it is going to get impacted the way Congress, which was an upper caste party, started appeasing to the Pichhalas also and to the Dalits also, and they ended up being nowhere. There is no proposition that the Congress party today has in the state of UP. This is why I believe, why ascending and rising Chandra Shekhar Azad and an MIM, even with a 4-5% of vote in a very closely contested election, might just prove to be decisive. They might not win any election, as I said. It can disturb the equations. Okay.
Alright. seconds to all final comments. Juhi Singh, you've been wanting to make a point. Quick, ma'am. seconds.

Yeah, that's an obnoxious comment by Mr. Sethi to say that there is actually some sort of an enmity or act coming between the Dalits and the pundits. So, if you do the PDM, sir, the socialist thinking has always been to work for the pitchers, Dalits, self-centred. So, all the people who are standing there waiting for you to, you know, really make the reforms which are needed. So, I don't see any problem there. And you said that, if we visit the Ram Mandir, then there will be an issue. You are hoping so, is it? But I think the people of UP are intelligent enough. I don't think people vote. by the fact whether we issue, whether we visit the Ram Mandir or we don't visit the Ram Mandir. I mean, democratically, India is a mature electoral society. So, you are making the same point from the other side, which Mr. Maris Prathan is making from this side, right? And Savajaradi Party is... Okay ma, seconds. Okay, Tuhin Sinha, seconds.

Look at the ambivalence, look at the confusion in the opposition camp. You know, just yesterday, they were tom-toming about, you know, they having the right to decide when to visit the temple. And now Juhi Ji is saying whether we visit the temple or not. It is this ambivalence, this confusion, this diffidence, which the voter will not want to see on the voting day. So let me tell you, you know, this announcement of the unnatural alliance today is the clearest sign yet that it will be a one-sided election very clearly, you know, reminiscent of a election. There is no other way. I am seeing this election. But yes, there is complete panic in the opposition camp, and there is complete therein, complete dissent.
Okay. seconds, Ashutosh, quickly.

I see the panic in the other camp. and especially the fight between the Delhi and the Lucknow. So that is why it is said that lakh votes have been deleted from the voter list. And Mr. Yogi Adityanath is extremely worried today. See, the reality today is that there is a tough contest in UP. There's no doubt about it. Chandrasekhar Azad, you know how much he got in vote share. In got vote share. Now imagine. Why these tidbits of political formations suddenly join together? Because the fight is very tough between these two political formations. And if or votes are either this way or that way, we will decide the elections.
